subject: Q3 renewal: supplemental top-up & retro usage reconciliation
messages:
From: Kate Dobson <kate.dobson@storix.com>

Cc: procurement@storix.com; Andrew Li <andrew.li@storix.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 renewal: supplemental top-up & retro usage reconciliation

Hi David —

Thanks again for the Q2 handoff. We finished our internal usage review and see a ~22% overage vs the committed capacity in May and June due to a billing spike from our experimental inference batch. We have two asks as we head into renewal:

1) Can Redwood provide a detailed reconciliation (per-day token/hours) for 2027-05-01 to 2027-06-30? We've attached our internal export.
2) We are open to a one-time top-up to cover the retroactive usage, but need clarity on the calculation and whether credits or amortized charges are an option for the renewal contract.

I've attached our CSV and a suggested draft amendment (for internal review). Can we set a short call early this week to align? Procurement is looped in.

Thanks —
Kate Dobson
Head of Platform, Storix Systems
kate.dobson@storix.com

Attachments: usage_breakdown_Q2.csv, draft_amendment_v2.docx

Subject: Re: Q3 renewal: supplemental top-up & retro usage reconciliation

Hi Kate —

Appreciate the details and the draft. I'll own the reconciliation and proposed settlement mechanics. Quick notes before our call:

- We can run a per-day export for the requested window; I'll attach our token/hour roll-up and spike analysis.
- Options we typically offer: one-time invoice for excess, credit offset against renewal, or amortized charge spread across the next 3 billing cycles. Each has a slightly different recognition/tax/PO implication — procurement please advise which is easiest on your side.
- For renewal sizing: if you expect sustained load, we can propose a tiered commit with burst buffer to avoid repeat true-ups.

I'm available Tue 27 Jul 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 28 Jul 14:30–15:00 PT. Which works? Marissa/Ben/Laura — looping you for numbers and approval bandwidth.

Cheers,
David Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

David / team —

Thanks. Tue morning conflicts here; Wed 14:30 PT works. Procurement notes: prefer credit offset if possible (simpler accounting), but can accept a one-time invoice if we get it before our renewal execution on Aug 10 so it can be included in the PO.

Andrew — are you okay with credit offset? If not, procurement will request payment terms net 45 for a one-time invoice.

See you Wed.

Kate
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Dobson <kate.dobson@storix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@storix.com
Date: Mon, 01 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal: supplemental top-up & retro usage reconciliation

Kate / Andrew / Procurement —

Summary and agreed path from today's call:

1) Reconciliation: Redwood delivered the per-day token & GPU-hour roll-up for 2027-05-01–2027-06-30 (see attached). We validated the ~22% overage and isolated a single job on 2027-05-17 that caused the spike.

2) Settlement option selected: credit offset against your Aug 10 renewal (Storix accepts credit rather than a separate invoice). Credit amount = $27,450 per our one-time calc (details in invoice_proposal_5781.pdf).

3) Renewal amendment: we'll add a one-line amendment to the MSA documenting the credit and an updated committed capacity block for Q3 with a 20% burst buffer. Draft amendment attached (draft_amendment_v2.docx).

4) Next steps and owners:
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare the final credit note and update the renewal quote with the amended commit.
- Redwood (Ben): confirm that the credit shows as a line-item on the renewal quote and that accounting can apply it prior to PO issuance.
- Storix (Andrew): share PO or confirmation once the renewal is approved on Aug 10.

We will proceed to generate the credit note and revised quote today so Storix can include it with procurement. If anything changes on timing, ping me directly.

Thanks — glad we found a straightforward path here.

David Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: invoice_proposal_5781.pdf, draft_amendment_v2.docx, usage_breakdown_Q2.csv
